about.intro_content: Prof. Hua Wang is a Professor in the Department of Hematological Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, specialising in molecular stratification diagnosis and precision treatment of hematological tumors.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Wang has made innovative contributions to understanding recurrence, drug resistance mechanisms, and optimisation of clinical treatment in hematological tumors, achieving 5-year survival rates that reach internationally leading levels for treated patients. Findings from his individualised treatment and prognosis research are cited in the American NCCN guidelines and are used worldwide. His research on extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma has examined PD-L1 upregulation via the LMP1/NF-κB pathway, CD30 as a prognostic indicator, and tumour-associated macrophages as markers of poor prognosis.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Hua Wang

items.question: Does Prof. Hua Wang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to hematological tumors at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Wang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Wang specialises in molecular stratification diagnosis and precision treatment of hematological tumors, particularly extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Wang's research reflected in international treatment guidelines?
items.answer: Yes. Findings from Prof. Wang's individualised treatment and prognosis research for hematological tumors are cited in the American NCCN guidelines and used worldwide.

items.question: How does molecular stratification improve treatment for blood cancers?
items.answer: Molecular stratification identifies subtypes and risk factors within a hematological tumor, allowing more individualized and precise treatment selection, which Prof. Wang's research has shown can improve 5-year survival outcomes.
